requirements.subject: ent:declaration
requirements.condition: general case, except where clause 5.3 requires declaration before use
requirements.canonical: A declaration MAY be made in any order relative to other declarations, subject to the declaration-before-use rule for test case definitions, functions, altsteps and statement blocks.
requirements.original: Generally, the order in which declarations can be made is arbitrary.

ambiguity.issue: "Generally" does not say where the arbitrary order applies; later sentences restrict it inside testcases, functions, altsteps and statement blocks. Chose the reading that the general rule is limited by those restrictions.
readings: A declaration MAY be made in any order anywhere, except that local definitions SHALL be declared before their first use.
A declaration MAY be made in any order only in the module definitions part and in a component type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:declaration
requirements.condition: the declaration is inside a statement block (e.g. a function body or a branch of an if-else statement)
requirements.canonical: A declaration inside a statement block MAY occur at any place where a statement can occur.
requirements.original: Inside a statement block, such as a function body or a branch of an if-else statement, declarations (if any) can occur at any place where a statement can occur.

requirements.subject: ent:declaration
requirements.canonical: A declaration in the module definitions part MAY be made in any order.
requirements.original: Declarations in the module definitions part and in a component type definition may be made in any order.

requirements.subject: ent:declaration
requirements.canonical: A declaration in a component type definition MAY be made in any order.
requirements.original: Declarations in the module definitions part and in a component type definition may be made in any order.

requirements.subject: ent:declaration
requirements.condition: the declaration is inside a testcase definition, function, altstep or statement block
requirements.canonical: A declaration inside a testcase definition, function, altstep or statement block SHALL be given before its first place of usage.
requirements.original: However inside test case definitions, functions, altsteps, and statement blocks, all required declarations shall be given before their first place of usage.

ambiguity.issue: "test case definitions" is used for the TTCN-3 testcase definition; the glossary term "test case" denotes the abstract test case, the language element is `testcase`.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: A local variable, local timer or local constant SHALL NOT be used before it is declared.
requirements.original: This means in particular, local variables, local timers, and local constants shall never be used before they are declared.

requirements.subject: ent:label
requirements.canonical: A label IS the only exception to the rule that declarations inside testcase definitions, functions, altsteps and statement blocks SHALL be given before their first place of usage.
requirements.original: The only exceptions to this rule are labels.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A `goto` statement MAY reference a label that occurs later in the same statement block (forward reference).
requirements.original: Forward references to a label may be used in goto statements before the label occurs (see clause 19.8).

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module MAY be parameterized.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to parameterize modules, templates, functions, altsteps and testcases.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template MAY be parameterized.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to parameterize modules, templates, functions, altsteps and testcases.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function MAY be parameterized.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to parameterize modules, templates, functions, altsteps and testcases.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be parameterized.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to parameterize modules, templates, functions, altsteps and testcases.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A testcase MAY be parameterized.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to parameterize modules, templates, functions, altsteps and testcases.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the parameterizable object allows the corresponding kind of formal parameter (see table 2)
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter MAY be a value, a template, a timer or a port.
requirements.original: Values, templates, timers, and ports may be used as actual parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:type-parameterization
requirements.canonical: Type parameterization IS NOT part of the TTCN-3 core language; it is defined in the optional package [i.12].
requirements.original: NOTE: Type parameterization for TTCN-3 is defined in the optional package [i.12].

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL be a value parameter (value parameterization only).
requirements.original: **module** Value parameterization Static at start of runtime all basic types, all user-defined types and address type.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: Module parameterization IS static parameterization that takes place at the start of runtime.
requirements.original: **module** Value parameterization Static at start of runtime all basic types, all user-defined types and address type.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL be of a basic type, a user-defined type or the address type.
requirements.original: **module** Value parameterization Static at start of runtime all basic types, all user-defined types and address type.

ambiguity.issue: Rows for function/altstep/testcase list component type, port type and default separately from user-defined types, so it is unclear whether "all user-defined types" for modules includes component types. Chose the reading that component, port and default types are excluded.
readings: A module parameter SHALL be of a basic type, a user-defined type other than a component type or port type, or the address type.
A module parameter SHALL be of a basic type, any user-defined type (including component types) or the address type.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template MAY have value parameterization and template parameterization.
requirements.original: **template** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address type parameterization and template.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: Template parameterization IS dynamic parameterization that takes place at runtime.
requirements.original: **template** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address type parameterization and template.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter belongs to a template formal parameter list
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a template SHALL be of a basic type, a user-defined type, the address type, or a template formal parameter.
requirements.original: **template** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address type parameterization and template.

ambiguity.issue: The column "Allowed types" lists "template", which is a kind of parameter, not a type.

improper_terms.used: template (as a type in formal parameter lists)

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function MAY have value parameterization and template parameterization.
requirements.original: **function** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address parameterization type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: Function parameterization IS dynamic parameterization that takes place at runtime.
requirements.original: **function** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address parameterization type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter belongs to a function formal parameter list
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a function SHALL be of a basic type, a user-defined type, the address type, a component type, a port type or the default type, or be a template or timer formal parameter.
requirements.original: **function** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address parameterization type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

ambiguity.issue: The column lists "template" and "timer" (kinds of parameters) as types and "default" instead of "default type".

improper_terms.used: template (as a type in formal parameter lists)

requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY have value parameterization and template parameterization.
requirements.original: **altstep** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address parameterization type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: Altstep parameterization IS dynamic parameterization that takes place at runtime.
requirements.original: **altstep** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address parameterization type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter belongs to an altstep formal parameter list
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of an altstep SHALL be of a basic type, a user-defined type, the address type, a component type, a port type or the default type, or be a template or timer formal parameter.
requirements.original: **altstep** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types, all user-defined types, address parameterization type, component type, port type, default, template and timer.

ambiguity.issue: The column lists "template" and "timer" (kinds of parameters) as types and "default" instead of "default type".

improper_terms.used: template (as a type in formal parameter lists)

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A testcase MAY have value parameterization and template parameterization.
requirements.original: **testcase** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types and of all user-defined types, parameterization `address type, component type and template.`

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: Testcase parameterization IS dynamic parameterization that takes place at runtime.
requirements.original: **testcase** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types and of all user-defined types, parameterization `address type, component type and template.`

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter belongs to a testcase formal parameter list
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a testcase SHALL be of a basic type, a user-defined type, the address type or a component type, or be a template formal parameter; port, default and timer formal parameters SHALL NOT be used.
requirements.original: **testcase** Value and template Dynamic at runtime all basic types and of all user-defined types, parameterization `address type, component type and template.`

ambiguity.issue: The row omits port type, default and timer, which the function/altstep rows allow; whether the omission is a prohibition is implied, not stated. "template" is also listed as a type. Chose the reading that omitted kinds are not allowed.
readings: A testcase formal parameter SHALL NOT be a port, default or timer parameter.
The table lists only typical testcase formal parameter types; port, default or timer parameters are not explicitly forbidden.

improper_terms.used: template (as a type in formal parameter lists)

requirements.subject: ent:signature
requirements.canonical: A signature IS NOT a parameterizable object in the sense of table 2, because a signature only declares parameters.
requirements.original: NOTE: Signatures are not shown in the table, because a signature declares parameters only.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: A template for a signature CAN be parameterized.
requirements.original: The templates for the signatures can be parameterized, however.
